This pathway develops the mathematical independence needed for advanced
quantitative work. You will alternate among theory, complete manual solutions,
computation, and interpretation. Definitions and hypotheses matter as much as
answers; computational output must be explained and checked.

[Start here](start-here.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Take the diagnostic](diagnostic.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## How the pathway works

1. **Orient.** Read [Start here](start-here.qmd) and set up a sustainable study
   routine.
2. **Diagnose.** Use the low-stakes [diagnostic](diagnostic.qmd) to locate gaps.
3. **Build foundations.** Study algebra and mathematical computing before or
   alongside the proof- and model-intensive courses.
4. **Deepen structure.** Connect linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics,
   probability, statistics, and differential equations.
5. **Integrate.** Use cumulative mixed practice so the method is not revealed by
   a chapter heading.

## Standard of mathematical work

A strong solution should identify the governing definition or theorem, verify
its hypotheses, show a logically complete argument, distinguish exact results
from approximations, and interpret the answer in context. Examples are not
proofs; plots are evidence, not proof; software output is a claim to be checked.
